title: Constant derived etale cohomology vanishing agrees with Ext cohomology vanishing on an isomorphic scheme
statement: For schemes X,Y [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], an isomorphism e : X to Y, an arbitrary abelian group M, and a natural number n, the derived etale cohomology H^n(RGamma(X,M[0])) [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology, def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf] is a zero object if and only if the Ext-defined Sheaf.H of the constant sheaf M on Y in degree n is a subsingleton. There are no finiteness, affineness, normality or field hypotheses.

source.place: Lemma 09ZC, implicit transport in the first sentence; comparison of definitions is the existing lem-weil-pbc-sheafH-ext-derived-comparison (Derived Categories 015A, 05TI, 06XR; Etale Cohomology 03Q5).

proof.text: For the inverse scheme isomorphism e.inv, cohomologyEquiv identifies H of the constant sheaf on X with H of its pullback to Y. upperStarConstantSheafIso identifies this pullback with the constant sheaf on Y; applying Sheaf.functorH.mapIso gives an additive equivalence. Compose these equivalences to obtain eH.

Choose the natural isomorphism supplied by Scheme.nonempty_sheafH_extDerivedIso X n. Its component at the constant sheaf identifies Sheaf.functorH.obj with derived cohomology of the single complex. A derived zero object therefore gives a subsingleton H on X by AddCommGrpCat.subsingleton_of_isZero. Transfer along eH.symm. Conversely transfer a subsingleton H on Y along eH, apply AddCommGrpCat.isZero_iff_subsingleton, and transport the zero object back along the component isomorphism.
